claims.text: Coupling CALPHAD phase-diagram calculations with machine-learning-enabled high-throughput screening can efficiently predict intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-density RHEA compositions.
RHEAs occupy a broad compositional space involving multiple principal refractory elements, often in equimolar or near-equimolar ratios.
The phase stability, lattice distortion, and deformation mechanisms of the starting refractory alloy space are not optimized by trial-and-error or solely thermo-kinetic approaches.
CALPHAD can be used to evaluate phase stability and potential precipitate formation in the candidate RHEAs.
Machine learning can rapidly screen the large RHEA compositional space and identify promising candidates.
Targeted high-throughput synthesis and testing can validate candidates selected by the computational workflow.
Elevated-temperature and aerospace-relevant conditions are appropriate application conditions for RHEAs.
Tensile testing and TEM/SEM characterization can verify ductility and phase distribution in the selected alloys.
The selected compositions will form controlled coherent intermetallic precipitates and exhibit useful lattice distortion from atomic-size mismatch.
Coherent precipitates and lattice distortion obstruct dislocation motion.
Avoiding brittle phase formation is necessary to retain ductility while increasing strength.
The integrated method predicts compositions that optimize the balance between solid-solution strengthening and precipitation hardening.
Balancing solid-solution strengthening and precipitation hardening enhances strength without sacrificing ductility.
The integrated design method can keep the alloy density relatively low.
Candidates identified by the integrated method will have higher yield strength, greater ductility, and lower density than conventionally designed alloys.
The predictive accuracy of CALPHAD and machine-learning models is limited by the quality and range of their input data.
Extrapolation to RHEAs with substantially different oxidation behavior is uncertain.
Long-term phase stability, oxidation resistance, and precipitate-morphology evolution under service conditions require experimental confirmation.
